thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — Increased KMS latency and 503s observed for GCP KMS in europe-west1. Affected: service startups (signing), live request signing. Error spike starting 2026-03-15T10:02:00Z. Paging oncall.
ops-bot: Paging @priya.k (SRE oncall) :rotating_light: — check startup/signing failures in logs.
priya.k: I’m on it. Looking at ingress and instance startup errors now. Early look: a lot of `KMS_UNAVAILABLE` and `deadline exceeded` from kms.googleapis.com.
jamal: Confirming — seeing startup tasks stuck waiting for keyring access, retries saturating worker threads.
priya.k: Impact: new pods in europe-west1 failing init (sidecar signing) causing 503/502 for customers on initial requests. Some long-lived services are ok because they already had cached keys.
maeve: Is this limited to europe-west1?
priya.k: So far yes — europe-west1 primarily. I see elevated latencies for kms.googleapis.com in our monitoring, high error rate visible in cloudtrace.
dave.m: Queuing note: client SDK does 3 quick retries then marks instance unhealthy. That fast retry loop is amplifying failures.
jamal: Immediate mitigation idea: increase client retry backoff and allow startup to continue without blocking on KMS for a short window (defer signing until ready).
priya.k: Agreed. Two-step plan: 1) Hotfix config to make sidecar tolerate KMS timeouts at startup (fallback to delayed signing). 2) Add aggressive exponential backoff and jitter to SDK (avoid thundering herd).
maeve: Do we have a way to warm keys locally so mid-flight requests succeed?
dave.m: We have cached ephemeral keys in Vault for some fleets — can enable cache-first mode for these clusters while KMS recovers. Requires config push.
ops-bot: Running runbook step: enable kcache fallback = true for cluster europe-west1 (command below).
```
# enable ephemeral key cache fallback
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/signing-sidecar KCACHE_FALLBACK=true --context=gke-europe-west1
```
priya.k: Applying that now to signing-sidecar daemonset (rolling update set to maxUnavailable=1). Pushing patch to make startup non-blocking in parallel.
jamal: Noted. Also opening ticket with GCP support — escalating KMS/Cloud KMS latencies. Tagging cloud-support.
cloud-support: Received. GCP: Case #CS-2026-3579 — investigating regional control plane degradation affecting KMS; will update within 30m.
maeve: Customer impact summary for now: intermittent 502/503 on initial requests for some tenants in eu region over last 12 minutes. No data loss reported. Adding to incident status page.
priya.k: Live mitigation checklist executed: - enabled KCACHE_FALLBACK - increased SDK retry backoff to base 500ms, max 8s - 0-downtime restart of signing-sidecar with non-blocking init - routed new traffic to eu-west2 for critical customers (migration toggle).
dave.m: Code snippet we rolled (hotfix):
```
// tolerate KMS timeouts during startup
if (!kms.ready() && env.KCACHE_FALLBACK == "true") {
  log.info("KMS unavailable; enabling local cache fallback for startup")
  signingService.enableLocalCache()
} else {
  signingService.blockUntilKeyAvailable(timeout=30000)
}
```
priya.k: After config change we see new pods coming up successfully. Error rate for signing down from 45% -> 8% over 12 minutes.
jamal: Still seeing some spikes in requests that require immediate KMS access — for those we've toggled traffic to eu-west2 as fallback.
maeve: Any concern about cache serving stale keys / security? What TTL are we using?
dave.m: Cache TTL is 5m by default. For emergency mode we keep it strict (5m) and force revalidation once KMS healthy. Documented in runbook.
priya.k: Notifying account teams and posting on status page draft: "We are investigating increased KMS latencies in GCP europe-west1 that caused intermittent startup and signing errors for some services. Mitigations applied; partial recovery observed. Working with GCP on root cause."
ops-bot: statuspage update published to internal incident channel and external status page (under maintenance).
cloud-support: GCP update: "We are seeing elevated control plane latency due to regional networking issue impacting KMS frontends. Engineers are rolling mitigations; no ETA yet for full restoration."
jamal: Next steps: 1) Keep KCACHE_FALLBACK enabled until GCP confirms healthy 2) Patch client SDK to exponential backoff and bump retry ceiling 3) Postmortem: consider adding multi-region KMS routing and local key cache warm at boot 4) Add detection alert for KMS startup failures specifically.
maeve: I'm taking the handoff for the next 4 hours. @priya.k please collect logs and timeline for the postmortem. @dave.m please coordinate the SDK patch PR and fast rollback plan.
priya.k: On it. Capturing timeline: incident start 2026-03-15T10:02Z; KCACHE_FALLBACK enabled 2026-03-15T10:08Z; traffic routed to eu-west2 for some tenants 10:12Z; error rate reduced by 10:20Z.
dave.m: Will open PR with retry/backoff improvements and integration test for startup path by EOD.
maeve: Notifying legal/product about customers impacted and preparing communication for those with committed SLAs. No major revenue incidents yet, just increased error rates.
priya.k: Logging follow-up actions into the incident tracker: - postmortem owner: priya.k - SDK patch owner: dave.m - infra change to multi-region KMS failover: jamal
ops-bot: Incident: set status = "mitigated" (partial) — monitoring for full recovery.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (partial mitigation) — KMS errors reduced; continue monitoring.
maeve: I'll stay on watch and update when GCP gives final resolution. Handoff complete to @maeve. :white_check_mark:
priya.k: Thanks team — good coordination. Will assemble postmortem and include recommendations: stricter startup timeouts, cache-first bootstrap, and multi-region signing strategy.
